---
title: "Space Syntax, decomposed"
toc: false
---

**Which design choices make Space Syntax differ from street-network analysis, by how much, and
where?** Tested on Copenhagen + Frederiksberg and the Mumbai island city, with every Space Syntax
measure reimplemented in Python and matched to depthmapX.

![Indre By, Colaba and Dharavi at the same scale](atlas/a13_windows.png)

## Key findings

| | Finding |
|---|---|
| 1 | At walking radii, metric closeness and Space Syntax integration (NAIN) are nearly unrelated (ρ ≈ 0 at 400 m in both cities). No single step explains the gap; the **normalisation** is the largest. |
| 2 | **Choice / betweenness is robust** across representations, engines and cleaning; integration / closeness is where the approaches part ways. |
| 3 | **Network cleaning** (junction consolidation) is a design choice as large as angular cost; consolidation stubs disturb the two engines in opposite directions. |
| 4 | **Map extent** matters for global measures, and **position matters more than size**. |
| 5 | Axial maps **generated from OSM centrelines do not reproduce** a hand-drawn axial map (ρ ≤ 0.28). |
| 6 | **Neighbourhoods differ more than cities**: within-city spread of agreement is an order of magnitude larger than the Copenhagen–Mumbai difference. |

## Method in one table

| Rung | Representation | Cost | Measures | Engine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | junction graph | metric | harmonic closeness, betweenness | cityseer |
| S1 | segment graph | metric | harmonic, NC²/TD, betweenness | cityseer |
| S2 | segment graph | angular | NC²/TD, betweenness | cityseer |
| S3 | straight pieces | angular (tulip-1024) | integration, choice, NAIN, NACH | depthmapX |
| S4 | generated axial lines | topological | integration HH, choice, intelligibility, synergy | depthmapX |

Adjacent rungs differ by one design choice; their rank agreement (Spearman ρ over interior
streets) measures what that choice does.

## Project

Part of a programme on space, movement and exposure in formal and informal cities:
**P1** Space Syntax decomposed (this site) · **P2** the invisible network (Dharavi's lanes) ·
**P3** pedestrian-weighted exposure. Author: Manish Bilore.
